correctness.rationale: The exact source integral is smooth near (q,r)=(1,0) and even in r. At r=0, the spherical moment identities E[t^2]=1/n and E[t^4]=3/(n(n+2)) give Psi_ss(0,0)=2(n-1)(n+1)/(n(n+2)). Expanding the source Poisson-gradient formulas at q=1 gives Psi_s(0,r)=((n-2)(n-1)(3n+2)/(n^3(n+2))) r^2+O(r^4). The implicit-function theorem yields q_n(r)=1-((n-2)(3n+2)/(2n^2(n+1)))r^2+O(r^4). Strict convexity then gives the objective deficit A_n^2/(2H_n) r^4+O(r^6), exactly the stated delta_n.

value.rationale: Strict anisotropy is a headline structural feature of the fresh exact Jacobian theory. The accepted result identifies the first quantitative deformation of the extremal derivative and reveals a two-scale phenomenon: shape anisotropy is quadratic in radius, while its determinant payoff is quartic. This supplies an exact local benchmark for the newly implicit minimizer and distinguishes geometric deformation from objective improvement.
